title: How the pipeline works
text: You did the research this week. Here's how to turn it into a video the world can actually watch using Claude and the Brutalist System in one sitting. Liam for Humanitarian's AI. Six steps, one

title: Put your week's work in one folder — that's the raw material
text: Sitting. Your week's folder goes in. The Brutalist System provides the tools. Claude code builds the video. You watch and revise, then you publish. That's the whole pipeline and every step happens today. Step one, put your week in a folder.

title: Email hr@humanitarians.ai for the Brutalist system and setup help
text: Notes, code, figures, data, the paper draft, screenshots, all of it. That folder is the raw material. Claude reads it to find the stories worth animating. One folder equals one conversation with the pipeline. Step two, get the Brutalist System.

title: Open Claude Code: caffeinate claude --dangerously-skip-permissions
text: Email hr@humanitarians.ai and you'll receive the toolkit and setup help. Step three, open Claude code in the folder that holds both your work and the Brutalist skills. The command is caffeinate Claude dangerously skip permissions. Caffeinate keeps your Mac awake through the render. The flag lets Claude run the whole pipeline without stopping for each permission. Step four,

title: Give Claude your specific prompt — name your project, result, and key idea
text: Give Claude the prompt with your specifics. Start from the generic seed, create a Claude explainer in the Liam voice for every video idea in this folder, then steer it. Name your project, name the result, name the figure worth showing, name the one idea you want a viewer to leave with. The specifics are what make it yours. And if you're using the Liam voice, tell Claude to have Liam say Liam for your name and Humanitarian's AI. Make it yours out loud. Step five, watch then ask for

title: Watch the video, then ask for changes in plain language
text: Changes. Claude builds the video. Watch it. Anything off, a wrong number, a pace that drags, a chart that should be a different chart, just tell Claude in plain language. Plain language in better video out. Iterate until it's right. Step six, publish to the channel. When

title: Publish to / @humanitariansai → Fellows Research playlist
text: It's ready, use Gorav's publishing script, get it from hr@humanitarians.ai to post your video to YouTube.com/athumanitariansai in the fellows research playlist. That's where your research explainer lives. Let's recap with Claude. Six steps to turn your research week into a published video. Your folder of notes, code, and figures, the Brutalist System from the email, Claude code in that folder with a specific prompt. Watch and revise, then publish to the fellows research playlist. Here's the prompt to run in your own session. Here's my folder of this week's research. Describe what you did. Create a Claude explainer in the Liam voice for every video idea in it with animated visualizations and infographics and have Liam say Liam for my name and humanitarian's AI. Fill in that bracket with one line about your own work. That's all Claude needs to start building. How to make explainer videos for your research Liam for humanitarian's AI.
